page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 31.0 GB of RAM, yielding 7.75 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The CPU features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for integer and tile operations.

Benchmark results indicate highly polarized performance characteristics. Single-core performance is a notable strength, with Geekbench single-core scores reaching 2258.0 (top tier, top 10%) and single-threaded text processing scoring 2843.0. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory subsystem performance are significantly weaker. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU score fall into the bottom 25%, while uncached memory read and write bandwidths are also weak. Redis SET operations are limited to 4.9 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio within its hardware class, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The primary tradeoff is the disparity between strong single-threaded execution and weak multi-core scaling, alongside lower uncached memory bandwidth. This profile makes the server appropriate for single-threaded applications, light database operations, text processing, and moderate web serving, but less optimal for highly parallelized compute-intensive tasks or memory-bandwidth-heavy applications.
